question: Which part of a neuron carries the nerve impulse away from the cell body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Axon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Axon** is a long, slender projection of a **nerve cell** or **neuron** that typically conducts electrical impulses known as **action potentials** away from the **cell body** (also known as the **soma**). ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• It serves as the primary transmission line of the nervous system, and as a bundle, axons help make up **nerves**.
 
• The axon originates from a specialized region of the cell body called the **axon hillock**, which acts as a junction where signals are integrated before being sent down the axon.
